This section examines how WRF weather fields, physics parameterizations, and initial and boundary conditions affect simulations of clouds and precipitation. Case selection, sensitivity experiments, and interpretation are documented as reproducible workflows.

The first series starts from the idealized 2-D squall-line case. After checking how vertical shear and the warm bubble shape convection, it swaps microphysics schemes and background aerosol, then prepares bin microphysics (fast SBM) for hygroscopic seeding experiments. The goal is to recompute the particle-size experiment of [Ren et al. (2025)](posts/article-review/2026-09-10-ren2025-particle-size/index.qmd) in 2-D WRF.

```text
1. Basic 2-D squall line       →  vertical shear · warm-bubble sensitivity
2. Microphysics comparison     →  fast SBM 2-D bug fix · maritime vs continental aerosol
3. (in progress) Ren et al. (2025) case setup  →  KCl hygroscopic seeding
```
